atoms.b: My name is Claudius Ptolemy and I was a Greek ((++astronomer carpenter)) working in Egypt in the 2nd century.
atoms.sound: My name is Claudeus toluhhmee and I was a Greek astronomer working in Egypt in the 2nd century.

atoms.b: My geocentric model of the ((++solar polar)) system placed the ((++Earth Venus)) in the centre, and was used for almost 1,500 years.

instruction.text: Drag the Earth and the Sun to the correct places in Ptolemy’s geocentric model.
instruction.sound: Drag the Earth and the Sun to the correct places in toluhhmee’s geocentric model.

atoms.b: My name is Nikolaus Copernicus and I was a Polish ((++astronomer astrologer)) working in the 16th century.
I went against the ideas of ((++Ptolemy Newton)) and was one of the first astronomers to create a model of the heliocentric solar system — with the ((++Sun Earth)) in its centre.

instruction.text: Drag the Sun, Jupiter and Saturn to the correct places in Copernicus’s heliocentric model.

finish.text: Uranus and Neptune were not discovered until 1781 and 1846 respectively. That’s why they are not in the models of either astronomer.

atoms.a: Which of the astronomers was correct about the structure of our solar system?
